hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an eligibility assessment for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand which children you're applying for Child Benefit. 

**Could you please tell me:**

1. **How many children** do you want to claim for?
2. **What is/are their name(s) and age(s)?**

This will help me guide you through the assessment properly, as the eligibility rules depend on the child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 16 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So we're looking at Child Benefit eligibility for your son **Alex, who is 16 years old**.

Since Alex is 16-19, I need to check whether he qualifies based on education or training requirements. Let me get the details for this part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In full-time education or training** (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Please let me know which applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He recently left education, actually. He's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex recently left education and has signed up with the careers service, I need to check whether he qualifies for a Child Benefit extension. Let me get the details on the extension eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! This is important. The rules state that if a child aged 16-17 has left education, they can still qualify for Child Benefit under a **20-week extension** if they've registered with a **qualifying service**. The qualifying services are:
- Government careers service
- Connexions
- Armed services

**A few clarifying questions:**

1. **Is Alex aged 16 or 17?** (You mentioned he's 16, just confirming)
2. **How long ago did he leave education?** (Was it within the last 20 weeks?)
3. **Has he registered with the local careers service** - is this a government careers service, or another type of service?

These details will determine if he qualifies for the 20-week extension.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is 16. He left school fairly recently - I'd say it's been a couple of months now. And yes, he registered with the government careers service, the one the school told us about.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex meets the conditions for the 20-week extension:

- ✓ He's 16 years old
- ✓ He left education a couple of months ago (well within the 20-week window)
- ✓ He's registered with the government careers service (a qualifying service)

This means he qualifies for the extension. Now I need to check one more important requirement: **whether Alex is working full-time**. If he's working full-time, he wouldn't be eligible for Child Benefit, even with the extension.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working 24 or more hours per week?** 

In other words:
- Is he working **less than 24 hours per week** or **not in paid work at all**? (If yes, he can proceed)
- Or is he working **24+ hours per week**? (If yes, he wouldn't be eligible)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now. He's just taking some time to figure out his next steps.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So Alex is not working at all, which means he passes that check. Now I need to verify one more thing - whether Alex is receiving certain benefits. Let me get the details on that requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)?
- Universal Credit?

If he's not receiving either of these, he can continue. If he is receiving one or both, he wouldn't be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not receiving those benefits. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - Alex is not working and is just exploring his options. Let me ask to be thorough:

**Is Alex currently in any apprenticeship program?** (For example, an Intermediate Apprenticeship, Advanced Apprenticeship, Higher Apprenticeship, Modern Apprenticeship, etc.)

If not, we can move on to the next check!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just registered with the careers service to work out what he wants to do.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me get the details on that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. The main question is:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If you do, that's the simplest path. However, if you don't, there are other special circumstances that might still qualify you (such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant living abroad). 

What is your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Now I need to check one more important thing - whether you have parental responsibility for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
To qualify for Child Benefit, you need to have parental responsibility for Alex. This means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. - at least an amount equivalent to the Child Benefit), OR
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement that covers Alex's upkeep

**Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which means you have parental responsibility for him. Now I need to check one final requirement - where Alex is located.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, is Alex's other parent, a grandparent, or any other person already receiving Child Benefit payments for him?

If not, we can move forward. If someone else is claiming, we need to know if you've agreed with them about the claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now, one final check - I need to confirm where Alex is located.

**Is Alex normally in the UK?** (Since you're in Manchester with him, I'd expect the answer is yes, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility requirements.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is here in the UK with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in the UK with you. Let me get the final details to complete the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just to confirm Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex:**
1. In hospital?
2. In local authority care?
3. Fostered (with a foster carer)?
4. Living normally at home with you?

I'm assuming he's living normally at home, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's living normally at home with me. Nothing out of the ordinary.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me get the final eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?** (For example, through fostering payments or other support)

I'm assuming the answer is no since he's living normally at home with you, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Based on all the information you've provided, I can now determine Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit. Let me compile the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **Great News! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

Based on my assessment, you meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex.

### **Why Alex Qualifies:**

1. **Age & Education Status:** Alex is 16 years old and recently left full-time education. Because he's registered with the government careers service, he qualifies under the **20-week extension rule**. This means he can continue to qualify for Child Benefit even though he's no longer in education.

2. **Work Status:** He's not working full-time (he's not working at all), so this doesn't disqualify him.

3. **Benefits:** He's not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right.

4. **Apprenticeship:** He's not in an apprenticeship program.

5. **Your Responsibility:** You live with Alex and support him, so you have parental responsibility.

6. **Residency:** You both normally live in the UK (Manchester).

7. **No Conflicts:** No one else is claiming for Alex, and the local council isn't paying towards his upkeep.

### **Important Information:**

⏰ **Remember:** The 20-week extension has a time limit. The extension ends after 20 weeks from when he left education, or when he turns 18, whichever comes first. You'll need to keep track of this deadline, as Alex will no longer qualify once it expires (unless he enters education or training in the meantime).

### **Next Steps:**

To claim Child Benefit, you'll need to:
- Contact HMRC to make a claim
- Provide evidence of Alex's age, education history, and registration with the careers service
- For more information, visit: [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

**Congratulations, and best of luck with Alex's next steps!**
